source.title: Spherical Boltzmann machines: a solvable theory of learning and generation in energy-based models
source.authors: Thomas Tulinski; S. Cocco; R. Monasson; Jorge FERNANDEZ-DE-COSSIO-DIAZ

page_placements.theme: Non-monotone risk along regularization or optimizer-noise axes

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports double-descent-like outcomes for generative metrics as regularization varies, but it does not test the claim versions’ specified axes or measures (model size, epochs, sample count, or effective complexity).
record.gate_note: The paper's own double-descent results measure generative reverse KL or test NLL as a function of regularization, not test error as a function of model size, epochs, or training-sample count. These related results are recorded with versions ["none"] and described under fits_no_version. Mentions of double descent in prior work are citations, not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper's own 'double descent' is a non-monotonic generative metric (reverse KL to a teacher, or test NLL) as a function of L2 regularization strength γ. It comes from an SBM theory plus a flow, an FVSBN and an RBM. None of the claim's versions uses regularization strength as the axis or a condensation transition as the peak location. No version is tested by test error versus model size, epochs or sample count, nor by an effective-complexity recount. Mentions of supervised and generative double descent elsewhere are citations only. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right, with three refinements. The authors derive the double descent in γ analytically for the SBM and tie the peak to the condensation (h≠0 to h=0) transition. They state it exists only for ηDD<η<∞, with the second descent collapsing in the MAP limit. They report qualitative reproduction in a spherical flow (MAP flat, Bayesian averaging needed), an FVSBN, and an RBM (bump visible even at MAP). They attribute the effect to the spherical constraint, absent in a Gaussian model. They make no claim about size-, epoch- or sample-wise test-error double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes regularization-dependent generative metrics in spherical Boltzmann machines and several other generative architectures; it does not use the original claim's model-size, epoch, or sample-size test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The SBM reverse-KL profile depends on posterior temperature: the first minimum disappears below ηDD≈1.342 for the stated teacher, while the MAP limit leaves a flat post-transition branch. The flow results vary with reweighting temperature. In the financial RBM, the bump shifts with training-set size, from γ≈3×10−2 at Mtrain=11428 to γ≈10−1 at Mtrain=1000.

fits_no_version.finding: In the SBM theory (rank-one teacher, ω*=2.5, K=2), the typical reverse KL versus γ has a minimum in the h≠0 phase and a spike at the condensation threshold γ=c1, then decreases. This occurs only for ηDD≈1.342<η<∞. Below ηDD the curve is monotone; in the MAP limit the post-transition branch is flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generative reverse-KL can be non-monotonic in regularization strength, peaking at a condensation transition, with the second descent arising from finite posterior temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: A normalizing flow on the sphere reproduces the reverse-KL bump at γ≈5–10, at the h≠0 to h=0 transition. The MAP curve is flat with no second descent; warming the reweighting temperature T moves γmin from ≈0.02 to ≈0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The regularization-axis bump in a generative flow requires Bayesian posterior averaging and grows with posterior temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: The FVSBN SWAG reverse-KL bump persists for K/N from 0.25 to 2, at +0.14 to +0.18 nats/N on the CW teacher and +0.22 to +0.27 on the Ising teacher. The peak shifts from γ≈0.30 (K≤8) to ≈1 (K≥16); amplitude is essentially K-independent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A regularization-axis bump in generative reverse KL persists across sample counts for low-effective-rank data, with its location tracking the top data eigenvalue.

fits_no_version.finding: A Gaussian–Bernoulli RBM on French 49-industry returns shows a test-NLL bump of ≈0.3 nats/day at the γ where σ2 of W collapses. The bump is visible in the MAP point estimate and shifts to larger γ as Mtrain falls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test NLL of an RBM can rise at the regularization strength where a secondary learned mode merges into the noise bulk.

fits_no_version.finding: A multivariate Gaussian analog has KL smooth in γ with no spike (App. E, Fig. 13). The bump is attributed to the spherical constraint.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The regularization-axis bump requires a non-conjugate partition function with a condensation transition.

record.problems: The paper does not directly test any listed claim version. Some related evidence is theoretical and relies on high-dimensional assumptions and heuristic saddle-point/DMFT derivations. The flow experiment uses N=30 and 30 seeds; the FVSBN uses N=16 and 10 seeds. The RBM evidence uses one fixed data split and 8 training seeds. Several curve values are available only in figures, and the paper reports aggregate rather than per-condition bump amplitudes for the FVSBN.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own double-descent results identified. Prior-work results mentioned in the introduction were excluded because they are cited rather than produced by this study. Individual plotted coordinates not described numerically in the text remain figure-only.

untested.parts: No sweep of deep-network size and no interpolation threshold. The only axis is regularization strength γ.
No test-error-versus-epochs curve. The training-time reverse KL of Fig. 6 dips, rises and settles (no second descent), and is an out-of-equilibrium sampling effect.
Sample count K or Mtrain is varied only to shift the γ-location of the bump (Fig. 17, Fig. 18). Test metric versus sample count at fixed γ near a threshold is not reported.
There is no capacity axis past an interpolation point. The peak sits at a condensation (h≠0 to h=0) transition in γ.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epoch and sample axes. The γ-peak is tied to a retarded-learning threshold γ∼ηc1², which is not the version's measure.

Label noise, multiple peaks and disappearance under optimal regularization are not tested. Regularization is itself the swept axis. The DD depends on posterior temperature η, which is not label noise.

missing.what: Gaussian-baseline comparison showing no spike in KL versus γ (a null result for the related finding)
Reverse KL during training dips then rises and settles higher at low sampling rate ν. This is a training-time curve that a V2 comparison might seek, but it is not double descent.
missing.versions: none (adjacent to V2, does not test it)

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to 'none' with state cannot_determine for the claim versions. No row needs correcting. The RBM result contrasts with the SBM and flow: there the bump appears without posterior averaging. Regularization strength could be read as an inverse capacity axis for V4. However, the peak is at a condensation threshold rather than an interpolation threshold, and the authors do not frame it as capacity, so no version verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure test error over deep-network model size or identify an interpolation threshold.
The paper does not measure test error over training epochs.
The paper does not test whether increasing sample count near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
The paper varies regularization in generative models, not capacity across model classes past an interpolation point.
The paper does not propose or test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.

The paper studies posterior-temperature dependence and regularization-dependent generative metrics, but does not test label-noise or variance as the driver, multiple descent peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not recount complexity by an effective number of parameters or test whether that makes a second descent an ordinary U-shape.

relation.reason: The study discusses established double descent and develops a related regularization-axis phenomenon without testing or using a catalog claim version.

tranche.reason: The reported double descent concerns generative metrics versus regularization strength and a condensation transition, rather than an interpolation threshold along capacity, epochs, or sample count. It does not test V1–V7.

source_check.notes: The source is internally inconsistent about temperatures: prose and caption specify T=5, while the extracted Figure 16 legend lists 0.2, 1, 2, 10 and 100. T=5 is text-supported, but its plotted curve identity needs clarification.

statements.correction: Reverse-KL bump: γ≈5–10. MAP curve: flat across the h≠0 phase; no second descent. γmin: ≈0.02 near MAP; ≈0.5 at T=5.
statements.problem: The numerical claims are explicit in Appendix F.2.1 and Figure 16, but MAP flatness is stated only for the h≠0 phase.
